cards.title: Hero copy reframed around craftsmanship, not just product features
cards.summary: One sandal brand rewrote its entire hero section around artisan leather sourcing and handcrafted quality, producing a reported 77K monthly incremental lift.
cards.use_when: You are rewriting above-the-fold copy for a product with a verifiable quality or provenance story (material sourcing, handmade process, craftsmanship) that current copy ignores.
steps: Audit the current hero copy: check whether it describes what the product does or how it is made and where materials come from.
Rewrite the whole hero block, not one line. Reframe it around the distinctiveness story: where the leather or material is sourced, that it is handcrafted, and why the quality is high.
Anchor the claim in specifics the brand can substantiate (sourcing location, handcrafted process) rather than generic quality adjectives.
Measure revenue per visitor, not just conversion rate, so a quality-led story is not credited by price discounting.
caveats: The 77K monthly incremental figure is the presenter's reported client result and not a promised benchmark.
The account is from a workshop transcript; test duration and sample size are not stated.
Quality narrative works only where the brand can genuinely back the claim; unverifiable craft claims risk trust and compliance issues.

cards.title: Use a free CRO growth plan as a lead offer for agency services
cards.summary: Offer a no-obligation free comprehensive CRO growth plan delivered on a call, with a limited-number scarcity frame and a QR code / short link to a Typeform qualification form.
cards.use_when: You are an agency or consultant selling CRO services and want a lead magnet that demonstrates expertise without requiring the prospect to commit to a paid engagement.
steps: Create a landing/qualification form asking for store URL, sessions and basic brand facts so you can prepare a relevant plan before the call.
Promise a specific deliverable: a free comprehensive CRO growth plan with recommended actions tailored to the brand's size, framed around profit per visitor and revenue, with no obligation to hire.
Limit the number of plans available and say so explicitly to create urgency; the source frames it as a limited quantity.
Deliver the plan on a booked call and let the prospect implement it themselves or hire you.
Use a QR code and a short memorable URL during live workshops or replays so mobile viewers can sign up immediately.
caveats: This is an agency lead-generation offer, not an ecommerce purchase funnel; transferable parts are the free high-value deliverable, qualification form and scarcity framing, not the CRO content itself.
Scarcity must be real or the tactic damages trust; 'hundreds of people on the call' framing assumes a live event.
The transcript is promotional and does not show close rates or plan-to-client conversion.

cards.title: Decide CRO depth by monthly session volume
cards.summary: Under 300,000 monthly sessions, the biggest uplift usually comes from building focused landing pages; over 300,000 sessions with sufficient orders, comprehensive CRO — audits, data analysis and isolated AB tests — is most powerful.
cards.use_when: You are deciding how to allocate CRO effort for a store of a given size and need to choose between landing-page work and a full testing program.
steps: Count monthly sessions and orders; below the roughly 300,000-session mark, prioritize building dedicated landing pages because the source reports that is where smaller stores see the biggest uplift.

Above 300,000 sessions per month, with a good enough conversion rate and enough orders to quantify results, run comprehensive CRO: long audits, deep data analysis and isolated AB tests measured by incremental revenue per visitor.
Run small isolated AB tests and look for incremental increases in revenue per visitor rather than large simultaneous changes.
For brands above the threshold, keep landing-page work in the mix but treat comprehensive testing as the primary lever for revenue per visitor.
caveats: The 300,000-session figure is the presenter's practical benchmark, not a statistically derived threshold and not a universal rule.
The source does not define 'good enough conversion rate' or 'enough orders'.
Bandwidth, traffic mix and product type still affect which lever works; verify your own data before committing.
